prerequisites: Reinforce and review prior knowledge of Chemistry, Physics, Biology, Earth and Environmental Sciences.
Basic knowledge of the English language.

learning_outcomes.text: Introduce students to the complex world of environmental engineering, understanding the importance of environmental pollution phenomena in interrelated hydrological, atmospheric, and edaphological processes, and establish the bases for their control.
Develop basic knowledge and application of technologies for treating liquid effluents, atmospheric pollution, and solid waste within the framework of sustainable development.

Obtain an overview of environmental engineering, interrelating polluting processes following physical, chemical, biological, and geological laws, and establish control processes by applying engineering knowledge.
Knowledge of the main characteristics of the atmospheric environment, its main pollutants, their evolution in the atmosphere, and their adequate control and reduction.
Knowledge of mathematical estimation models and the use of computer programs to simulate atmospheric pollution processes, design emission control devices, and estimate, calculate, and measure them.
Acquisition of skills in expressing concentrations and changing units of pollutant substances.
Acquisition of skills in the evaluation and calculation of reactions aimed at reducing pollutant substances.
Knowledge of the properties of the aquatic environment, its polluting processes, and its adequate treatment, purification, and management.
Knowledge in sizing sedimentation processes with discrete sedimentation models.
Knowledge in sizing sedimentation processes with zonal sedimentation models, through the analysis of the sedimentation curve.
Knowledge in sizing solids separation by flotation processes.
Knowledge in sizing homogenization systems.
Knowledge in sizing biological wastewater treatment systems by activated sludge.
Knowledge in sizing biological sludge treatment systems by anaerobic digestion.
Knowledge of the properties of waste and the edaphic environment, its polluting processes, and its corresponding treatment.
Introduction to the environmental assessment of polluting activities.
Understand and interpret texts and data, developing skills for their concretization and clear and concise exposition.
Know the basic principles and application of environmental technologies and sustainability.
Use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for finding sustainable engineering solutions.
Design using graphic engineering techniques.
Actively collaborate with a group of people to achieve a common goal and develop multidisciplinary projects.
The aforementioned competencies.

syllabus_topics: Environmental Engineering. Nature and content.

The atmosphere. Pollutant dispersion. Structure and composition of the atmosphere. Radiation, photochemical processes, and biogeochemical cycles. Influence of wind on pollutant dispersion. Vertical temperature gradient. Topographic factors. Atmospheric pollution models. Diffusion models. Gaussian model. Dispersion coefficients and effective chimney height.
Atmospheric pollutants and main anthropogenic sources. Carbon oxides. Sulfur oxides. Nitrogen compounds. Halogens. Metals and metallic ions. Hydrocarbons and photochemical oxidants. Particles.

Control of atmospheric pollution. Introduction. Control of mobile combustion sources. Control of fixed pollutant emission sources: carbon monoxide and hydrocarbons, nitrogen oxides, sulfur oxides, and particles.

Characterization of wastewater. Organic pollutant parameters: COD, BOD. Solids: total solids, suspended solids, settleable solids, volatile solids. Inorganic pollutants: nitrogen, phosphorus, other inorganic pollutants. Physicochemical pollution parameters: conductivity, pH, color, temperature. Biological pollutants. Urban and industrial wastewater.
Pretreatment and primary treatment. Coarse treatment. Decantation. Flotation. Neutralization and homogenization. Other types of pretreatment and primary treatment.

Secondary treatment. Theoretical bases of biological treatments. Activated sludge. Bacterial beds or trickling filters. Biodiscs or rotating biological contactors. Lagooning. Anaerobic process. Other types of secondary treatment.

Sludge treatment and tertiary treatment. Conditioning. Thickening. Stabilization. Dehydration. Land application. Evacuation. Other types of sludge treatment. Nitrogen and phosphorus removal. Reverse osmosis. Chemical oxidation. Other types of tertiary treatment.
Waste. Agricultural, livestock, and forest waste. Industrial waste. Hazardous waste. Urban waste. Recycling. Incineration. Landfills. Other treatments.
Special treatment waste. Noise. Marine pollution. Sanitary waste. Radioactive waste. Noise. Marine pollution.

Soil contamination. Origin and nature. Metallic pollutants. Organic pollutants. Pesticides. Soil remediation. Containment and confinement techniques. Extraction and transfer techniques. Thermal purification. Chemical purification. Biological purification. Energy, water, and reagent requirements.
Environmental impact assessment of polluting activities. The environmental impact assessment. Parts of an environmental impact assessment. Regulations.
Resolution of practical environmental pollution questions, which may include practical cases in the form of problems, treatment sizing, or laboratory practices.

Atmospheric pollution simulation practices, using mathematical estimation models as permitted by current regulations, for determining atmospheric pollutants in immission or for preparing the corresponding emissions inventory.

Practical knowledge required: mathematical estimation models and use of computer programs for simulating atmospheric pollution processes, designing emission control devices, and estimating, calculating, and measuring emissions.
Practical knowledge required: acquisition of skills in expressing concentrations and changing units of pollutant substances.
Practical knowledge required: acquisition of skills in the evaluation and calculation of reactions aimed at reducing pollutant substances.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of sedimentation processes by grit removal.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of sedimentation processes with zonal sedimentation models, by analyzing the sedimentation curve.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of solids separation by flotation processes.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of homogenization systems.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of biological wastewater treatment systems by activated sludge.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of biological wastewater treatment systems by trickling filters.
Practical knowledge required: knowledge in the sizing of biological sludge treatment systems by anaerobic digestion.
teaching_methods: Lectures with active student participation (exposition, explanation, examples, problem-solving using IT support, blackboard, handouts, digital whiteboard, projector, video, PowerPoint).
Problem-solving sessions in small groups with personalized explanations and active student participation.
Practical sessions and case studies in small groups.
Tutor-led seminars, specialized conferences/presentations with active student participation.
Preparation, defense, and exposition of assignments.
Personalized student learning monitoring through tutorials.
Personal study of theory and problems/practices.
Preparation of practice reports, assignments, and/or problem sets proposed by the professor.

assessment_methods.method: Atmospheric pollution practices (using mathematical estimation models for pollutant determination or emissions inventory)
Wastewater treatment sizing assignment (based on a hypothetical discharge)
Free-topic assignment on any aspect of the course program

assessment_rules: The final grade is based on written theoretical-practical exams (70%), atmospheric pollution practices (10%), a wastewater treatment sizing assignment (10%), and a free-topic assignment (10%). Clarity in content exposition, work performed, and interest in the subject (participation, seeking to expand knowledge) will be valued. Recommended activities for passing include class attendance with active participation, completing proposed assignments and readings, engaging in autonomous study activities, and utilizing tutorials.
